subsection.text_before_clauses: Where the competent authority, in consequence of information in his possession, has reason to believe that specified circumstances relating to non-production of books, documents or electronic information, or undisclosed income or property exist, the approving authority may authorise an authorised officer to exercise specified search and seizure powers.

clause.text_before_sub_clauses: Any person to whom the specified summons or notice has been or may be issued—

sub_clause.text_before_children: Has omitted or failed to produce books of account, documents, electronic information or information on a computer system as required by the summons or notice.
Will not or would not produce books, documents or electronic information useful for or relevant to proceedings under the Income-tax Act, 1961 or this Act.

clause.text_before_sub_clauses: Any person is in possession of an asset or information relating to an asset representing wholly or partly income or property which has not been, or would not be, disclosed for the purposes of the specified tax laws.

sub_clause.text_before_children: Enter and search any building, place, vessel, vehicle or aircraft where specified assets, books, documents or electronic information are suspected to be kept.
Require a person controlling electronic books, records, information or a computer system to provide reasonable technical and other assistance, including access codes.
Break open locks or override computer-system access codes where necessary for exercising the search powers and access is unavailable.
Search a person suspected of concealing books, documents, electronic information, a computer system or an asset.
Place identification marks on books or documents and make or cause extracts or copies to be made, including from computer systems.
Make a note or inventory of assets and business stock-in-trade found during the search.
Seize books, documents, computer systems or assets found during the search, other than stock-in-trade of the business.

subsection.text_before_children: An income-tax authority having territorial jurisdiction over a place but not jurisdiction over the person may exercise powers under sub-section (1) where delay in obtaining authorisation from the authority having jurisdiction over that person may prejudice the interests of revenue.

Where specified books, documents, electronic information, computer systems or assets are suspected to be kept at a location not mentioned in the original authorisation, the specified income-tax authority may authorise the officer to exercise the powers under sub-section (1)(i) to (vii) at that location.

sub_clause.text_before_children: Where physical possession of a valuable article or thing, other than stock-in-trade, is not possible or practicable because of its volume, weight, physical characteristics or dangerous nature, the authorised officer may order the person controlling it not to remove, part with or otherwise deal with it without prior permission.
Such action by the authorised officer shall be deemed to be seizure of the valuable article or thing under sub-section (1)(vii).

Where seizure of books, documents, assets, bank lockers, bank accounts or computer systems is not practicable for reasons other than those in clause (a), the authorised officer may restrict the owner or person controlling them from removing or dealing with them without permission and may take steps to ensure compliance.
Such order shall not remain in force for more than sixty days from the date of the order.
Serving such an order shall not be deemed to constitute seizure under sub-section (1)(vii).

subsection.text_before_children: The authorised officer may requisition specified services to assist with the purposes specified in sub-sections (1) and (3).

clause.text_before_children: Any police officer or officer of the Central Government, or both.
Any approved person or entity in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

subsection.text_after_children: Every such officer, person or entity shall comply with the requisition.

subsection.text_before_children: During a search or seizure, the authorised officer may examine on oath persons possessing or controlling specified books, documents, assets or electronic information, persons having access to computer systems, or other persons present at the premises.

clause.text_before_children: Statements made during such examination may subsequently be used as evidence in proceedings under the Income-tax Act, 1961 or this Act.
The examination may extend beyond material found during the search to all matters relevant to an investigation connected with proceedings under the specified Acts.

subsection.text_before_children: Where a person is found during a search to possess or control books, documents, assets, electronic information or a computer system, or to have access to such computer system, specified presumptions may be made.

clause.text_before_children: The books, documents, information, asset or computer system may be presumed to belong to that person.
The contents of the books, documents, electronic information or computer system may be presumed to be true.
Signatures and handwriting appearing in books or documents may be presumed to be those of the persons they purport or reasonably appear to belong to.
A stamped, executed or attested document may be presumed to have been duly stamped, executed or attested by the person by whom it purports to have been done.
Electronic information purportedly exchanged between parties may be presumed to have been exchanged between those parties.

subsection.text_before_children: The authorised officer may provisionally attach property belonging to the assessee during the search or seizure or within sixty days from execution of the last search authorisation.

clause.text_before_children: The attachment may be made where the authorised officer records reasons that it is necessary in the interest of revenue and obtains the prescribed prior approval.
The provisional attachment shall remain valid for six months from the end of the month in which the order is made, with the applicable rules applying mutatis mutandis.

subsection.text_before_children: During a search or seizure, or within sixty days from execution of the last search authorisation, the authorised officer may refer property for valuation to a Valuation Officer or another specified approved valuer, requiring that person to—

clause.text_before_children: Estimate the fair market value of the property in the prescribed manner.
Submit the valuation report to the authorised officer or Assessing Officer within sixty days from receipt of the reference.

subsection.text: The provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 relating to searches and seizure shall, so far as applicable, apply to searches and seizures under this section.

subsection.text_before_clauses: The Board may make rules relating to search or seizure under this section, including procedures to be followed by the authorised officer—

clause.text_before_children: For obtaining ingress into a building, place, vessel, vehicle or aircraft to be searched where free ingress is unavailable.
For ensuring safe custody of seized books, documents, assets, electronic information or computer systems.

subsection.text_before_children: For this section, proceeding means a proceeding relating to any year under the Income-tax Act, 1961 or this Act that is pending when the search is authorised, was completed on or before that date, or may subsequently be commenced under this Act for any year.
